title: Power Management
description: Review of low-power modes, the energy budget, battery handling and behavior on brownout and power loss.

items.text: An energy budget exists per mode, and measured current matches it
items.hint: Measure with a power analyzer across a full duty cycle, not just in sleep.

items.text: The system enters its lowest usable sleep mode whenever it's idle
items.hint: E.g. FreeRTOS tickless idle. Check that nothing holds the clocks on.

items.text: Every wake-up source is known, and unexpected wake-ups are counted
items.hint: Spurious wake-ups are a common reason for short battery life.

items.text: Peripherals and external parts are powered down or put to sleep when unused
items.hint: Including sensors, radios and pull-ups on idle buses.

items.text: Debug builds that block sleep are not what's measured or shipped
items.hint: Debug interfaces often keep clocks running.

items.text: State of charge is estimated with a method suited to the chemistry
items.hint: Voltage alone is poor for Li-ion under load. Use a fuel gauge or coulomb counting.

items.text: Charging respects the cell's temperature and voltage limits
items.hint: Don't charge Li-ion below 0 °C. Firmware-controlled chargers need independent hardware protection.

items.text: Low-battery behavior is graceful: warn, save state, then shut down
items.hint: Shut down before brownout corrupts storage.

items.text: Shipping or storage mode keeps self-discharge within shelf-life targets
Power loss is detected early enough to finish critical writes
items.hint: Use the PVD or a supply monitor, and know the hold-up time from bulk capacitance.

items.text: The device recovers to a correct state after a power cut at any moment
items.hint: Automate cycles at random points (e.g. 1,000 cuts) and check state and storage each time.

items.text: Behavior on slow-rising and dipping supplies is tested
items.hint: Slow ramps and short dips can leave the MCU half-reset without a supervisor.
